THOUGHT: The patient is a young adult with 2 months of epigastric pain classically worse a few hours after meals (typical for duodenal ulcer pain). Upper endoscopy shows multiple duodenal ulcers, which raises concern for pathologic gastric acid hypersecretion rather than a single H. pylori or NSAID-related ulcer. Laboratory testing demonstrates marked hypercalcemia (Ca 13.2 mg/dL) without other medical history. A family history of similar symptoms in his father suggests an inherited syndrome. The combination of primary hyperparathyroidism (causing hypercalcemia) and a gastrin-secreting tumor (gastrinoma) producing multiple duodenal ulcers is highly suggestive of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) — MEN1 commonly causes parathyroid hyperplasia (hypercalcemia), pancreatic/duodenal neuroendocrine tumors including gastrinomas (Zollinger–Ellison syndrome), and pituitary tumors. Even without diarrhea or other findings, the constellation of hypercalcemia, multiple duodenal ulcers, young age, and positive family history makes MEN1 with a gastrinoma the most likely diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) with gastrinoma (Zollinger–Ellison syndrome) causing multiple duodenal ulcers and concurrent primary hyperparathyroidism.
